[[File:Jessica Fintzen MFO 2016.jpg|thumb|Fintzen at the [[Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics]], 2016]]
'''Jessica Fintzen''' is a German mathematician whose research concerns the [[representation theory]] of [[algebraic group]]s over the [[p-adic number|{{mvar|p}}-adic numbers]], with connections to the [[Langlands program]]. She is a professor at the [[University of Bonn]].

==Education and career==
Fintzen competed for Germany in the 2008 [[International Mathematical Olympiad]], earning a bronze medal,{{r|mo}} and earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from [[Jacobs University Bremen]] in 2011. She went to [[Harvard University]] for graduate study in mathematics, completing her Ph.D. in 2016.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation concerned the [[Moy–Prasad filtration]] and was supervised by [[Benedict Gross]].{{r|mg}}

After postdoctoral research at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], [[University of Michigan]], and [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], she became an assistant professor of mathematics at [[Duke University]] and was promoted to full professor there in 2022. She has also been Royal Society University Research Fellow and Lecturer at the [[University of Cambridge]] since 2020. In 2022 she became a full professor at the [[University of Bonn]].{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Fintzen won the 2018 Friedrich Hirzebruch Dissertation prize of the [[Studienstiftung|German Academic Scholarship Foundation]] and Theodor Pfizer Foundation,{{r|fh}} and the 2018 [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] Dissertation Prize.{{r|aw}} She was named as a [[Sloan Research Fellow]] in 2021.{{r|sf}} In 2022, Fintzen won the [[Whitehead Prize]], "for her groundbreaking work in representation theory, in particular as it relates to number theory via the (local) Langlands program".{{r|wp}} In 2024, she was awarded the [[Cole Prize|Cole Prize in Algebra]],<ref>[http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7257 Cole Prize in Algebra 2024]</ref> and EMS Prize "for her transformative work on the representation theory of p-adic groups, in particular for her spectacular proof that Yu’s construction of supercuspidal representations is exhaustive''".''<ref>{{Cite web |title=EMS {{!}} Fourteen prizes awarded to European mathematicians at the 9th ECM |url=https://euromathsoc.org/news/fourteen-prizes-awarded-to-european-mathematicians-at-the-9th-ecm-121 |access-date=2024-07-15 |website=euromathsoc.org |language=en}}</ref>
